understanding.emotion: I have decided, and I am ready to begin
understanding.bridge: What you are living with is what the texts call stuck and not starting, and that is where this week begins.
understanding.insight: Doubt is spending the energy you would use to begin.

situations.label: Everything in my life is changing at once

queries.hook: A fire lit by seeing what others achieved; the resolve to rise, gather your strength and take on what is yours to do.
queries.diagnose: Doubt and delay feed each other; waiting to feel ready keeps us stuck, and the unacted-on decision weighs more than the work.
queries.steady: No effort on the right path is ever wasted; even a little of it protects you and carries you forward.
queries.act: Rise and do the next right thing; act without waiting for certainty, and keep at it day by day.
queries.story: A story of someone who set out to build or win something that was theirs to do, met the first test, and kept going.

understanding.life_context: Working. Feels determined; closest to "I can't stay consistent" and "I keep procrastinating".

hook.speaker: Krishna
hook.setting: Krishna to Arjuna on why even the fulfilled keep working for the world.
hook.sanskrit: तस्मादसक्तः सततं कार्यं कर्म समाचर । असक्तो ह्याचरन्कर्म परमाप्नोति पूरुषः ॥
hook.line: So keep doing the work that needs doing, well and without clinging. That's how you rise.
hook.translation: Therefore, always do the work that has to be done, without attachment; by working without attachment a person reaches the highest.
hook.why: People copy what you do, not what you say; keep showing up.

prasang.title: Even the wise, even God, act for the world's sake
prasang.summary: The one content in the self has nothing left to gain, yet the wise, like Janaka and Krishna himself, keep working because others follow their example.
prasang.lesson: People copy what you do, not what you say; keep showing up.

alternates.speaker: Krishna
alternates.setting: Krishna answers Arjuna, who asks why he must act at all if understanding is higher.
alternates.sanskrit: नियतं कुरु कर्म त्वं कर्म ज्यायो ह्यकर्मणः । शरीरयात्रापि च ते न प्रसिद्ध्येदकर्मणः ॥
alternates.line: Do the work that's yours. Doing something beats doing nothing; even living needs action.
alternates.translation: Do your allotted work, for action is better than inaction. Even the maintenance of your body would not be possible without action.
alternates.why: Not acting is still a choice; do the work that is yours.

prasang.title: Why doing your duty without attachment is better
prasang.summary: Arjuna is confused and asks for one clear answer. Krishna says no one can stop acting, that repressing the body while the mind indulges is self-deception, and that action beats inaction.
prasang.lesson: Not acting is still a choice; do the work that is yours.

alternates.speaker: Krishna
alternates.setting: Krishna on duties by nature and finding fulfilment in your own work.
alternates.sanskrit: सहजं कर्म कौन्तेय सदोषमपि न त्यजेत् । सर्वारम्भा हि दोषेण धूमेनाग्निरिवावृताः ॥
alternates.line: Don't abandon work that suits you just because it has flaws. Every undertaking has some, like fire has smoke.
alternates.translation: One should not give up the work suited to one's nature, Kaunteya, even if it has faults; for all undertakings are clouded by faults, as fire is by smoke.
alternates.why: Do the work that fits you, flaws and all, as an offering.
alternates.misuse: Not 'never change jobs'. It answers perfectionism, not a reason to stay where you're harmed.

prasang.title: Duties by nature, and their fruit
prasang.summary: After listing duties by varna, Krishna says one reaches perfection through one's own work done as worship, and that one's own path, though imperfect, beats another's, since every undertaking has flaws.
prasang.lesson: Do the work that fits you, flaws and all, as an offering.

verse.speaker: Krishna
verse.setting: Krishna to Arjuna on why even the fulfilled keep working for the world.
verse.sanskrit: तस्मादसक्तः सततं कार्यं कर्म समाचर । असक्तो ह्याचरन्कर्म परमाप्नोति पूरुषः ॥
verse.line: So keep doing the work that needs doing, well and without clinging. That's how you rise.
verse.translation: Therefore, always do the work that has to be done, without attachment; by working without attachment a person reaches the highest.
verse.why: People copy what you do, not what you say; keep showing up.

prasang.title: Even the wise, even God, act for the world's sake
prasang.summary: The one content in the self has nothing left to gain, yet the wise, like Janaka and Krishna himself, keep working because others follow their example.
prasang.lesson: People copy what you do, not what you say; keep showing up.

verse.meaning: Krishna speaks to Arjuna on the battlefield. He says that even those who are fully content and have nothing to gain still perform their duties. They do so because the world follows their example. The verse proposes that you could keep doing the work that needs doing, well and without clinging. This is how you rise.
verse.for_you: The work that needs doing is the one right in front of you, not the distant ideal.
verse.try_today: Do one small task at work without checking for praise.
verse.scene_line: You are on the field, and the next move is yours.
asks: How do I start when nothing feels finished?
How do I show up when I feel stuck?

verse.speaker: Vidula
verse.setting: Queen Vidula rouses her son Sanjaya, who lies defeated and despairing after losing his kingdom.
verse.sanskrit: सर्वेषां कर्मणां तात फले नित्यमनित्यता / अनित्यमिति जानन्तो न भवन्ति भवन्ति च अथ ये नैव कुर्वन्ति नैव जातु भवन्ति ते / ऐकगुण्यमनीहायामभावः कर्मणां फलम्
verse.line: Every result is uncertain. Some who try succeed and some don't. Those who never try never do.
verse.translation: The result of every action is uncertain. Knowing this, some people act and succeed, some do not. But those who never act never succeed at all.
verse.why: Past failure doesn't define you. Results are uncertain, but those who never try never succeed.

prasang.title: Vidula rouses her defeated son
prasang.summary: Kunti sends Yudhishthira the old story of Queen Vidula, who finds her son lying defeated after losing his kingdom. She shames, then reasons, then encourages him until he rises and fights for it again.
prasang.story_hook: A prince lay in bed after losing everything, until his mother walked in and refused to let him stay there.
prasang.lesson: Past failure doesn't define you. Results are uncertain, but those who never try never succeed.

verse.meaning: Queen Vidula finds her son Sanjaya lying defeated after losing his kingdom. She tells him the result of every action is uncertain. Some who try succeed and some do not. But those who never try never do. She says knowing this, you could still act. Past failure does not define you.
verse.for_you: You are lying in the quiet after a long day, feeling the weight of what has not started. You know the work is waiting. The uncertainty of the result does not belong to your worth. It is the price of beginning. The only true failure is to stay still.
verse.try_today: Notice one thing you keep delaying and name the first step.
verse.scene_line: You are lying in the quiet after a long day, feeling the weight of what has not started.
asks: What if I fail again tomorrow?
How do I start when the result is uncertain?

verse.speaker: Narrator
verse.setting: Angad plants his foot in Ravana's court and dares anyone to move it; no one can.
verse.sanskrit: भूमि न छाँड़त कपि चरन देखत रिपु मद भाग। कोटि बिघ्न ते संत कर मन जिमि नीति न त्याग ॥
verse.line: A good mind doesn't leave what is right, though a million obstacles come.
verse.translation: The monkey's foot would not leave the ground, and seeing it, the enemy's pride drained away; just as a good person's mind does not abandon what is right, though a million obstacles come.
verse.why: Under insult, keep your purpose; a steady mind does not leave what is right.

prasang.title: Angad in Ravana's court
prasang.summary: Ram sends Angad as envoy, asking him to speak so the work gets done and it does Ravana good too. In court Ravana insults Angad, his dead father and his lord. Angad bears it, remembering that a lion gains no glory by killing a jackal. At last he plants his foot and dares anyone to move it; no warrior can.
prasang.story_hook: Angad sat down in the enemy's court, and they began to insult his father.
prasang.lesson: Under insult, keep your purpose; a steady mind does not leave what is right.

verse.meaning: In the Ramcharitmanas, Angad stands in Ravana's court. Ravana has insulted him, his dead father, and his lord. Angad bears it, knowing a lion does not gain glory by killing a jackal. Then he plants his foot on the ground and challenges any warrior to move it. No one can. The narrator says the monkey's foot does not leave the ground, and seeing it, the enemy's pride drains away. A good person's mind does not abandon what is right, though a million obstacles come.
verse.for_you: Your mind wants to pull back because the ground feels shaky. But your purpose is still there, under your feet. Let your next small task be your foot on the ground. It does not have to move the whole mountain. It just has to hold.
verse.try_today: Plant your foot on the one task you can start right now.
verse.scene_line: You are in your own court, daring the ground to hold.
asks: How do I hold my ground when the path is not clear?
What is the one small thing I can plant my foot on?
How do I keep my mind steady when the obstacles feel huge?

verse.speaker: Yama
verse.sanskrit: यस्त्वविज्ञानवान्भवत्ययुक्तेन मनसा सदा । तस्येन्द्रियाण्यवश्यानि दुष्टाश्वा इव सारथेः ॥ यस्तु विज्ञानवान्भवति युक्तेन मनसा सदा । तस्येन्द्रियाणि वश्यानि सदश्वा इव सारथेः ॥
verse.line: Without understanding, the senses bolt like wild horses; with a steady mind, they run like trained ones.
verse.translation: For one who lacks understanding, whose mind is never held steady, the senses run out of control like a driver's wild horses. For one who has understanding, whose mind is always steady, the senses obey like good horses.
verse.why: Hold the reins of your mind, or your senses will drive for you.

prasang.title: The chariot of the self
prasang.summary: Yama pictures a person as a chariot: the self is the rider, the body the chariot, the intellect the driver, the mind the reins and the senses the horses. With a steady mind the horses obey; without it they bolt. He ends with the call to arise and wake.
prasang.lesson: Hold the reins of your mind, or your senses will drive for you.

verse.meaning: Yama is still speaking to Nachiketa, who has turned down all the worldly gifts. Yama is showing him the mechanics of the self. He says that without understanding, the senses bolt like wild horses. With a steady mind, they run like trained ones. The point is to hold the reins of your mind, or your senses will drive for you.
verse.for_you: You want to build a steady practice. The doubt that keeps you from starting is the wild horse. You do not need to tame it all at once. You only need to hold the reins for one minute today. The doubt will not leave.
verse.try_today: Hold the reins for one minute before you begin your work.
verse.scene_line: You are the driver, and the doubt is the wild horse waiting to bolt.
asks: How do I hold the reins when the horse is already running?

verse.speaker: Medhavin
verse.setting: A young man named Medhavin urges his father not to keep postponing what truly matters.
verse.sanskrit: श्वः कार्यमद्य कुर्वीत पूर्वाह्णे चापराह्णिकम् / नहि प्रतीक्षते मृत्युः कृतमस्य न वा कृतम्
verse.line: Do tomorrow's work today, and the afternoon's in the morning. Time doesn't wait for you to be ready.
verse.translation: Do tomorrow's work today, and the afternoon's work in the morning. Death does not wait to see whether your work is done or not.
verse.why: Life slips away while we stay busy. Do what matters now.
verse.misuse: About not postponing what matters, not about working nonstop.

prasang.title: Medhavin: the son who woke his father
prasang.summary: A father lays out the conventional path of study, family and ritual. His son Medhavin replies that days and nights fall like arrows and death takes people mid-task, so do tomorrow's work today and live truthfully now.
prasang.lesson: Life slips away while we stay busy. Do what matters now.

verse.meaning: Medhavin speaks to his father, who sits back, laying out the path of study and ritual as if there is endless time. Medhavin answers that days and nights fall like arrows, and death takes people mid-task. He tells him to do tomorrow's work today, and the afternoon's in the morning. Time does not wait for you to be ready. The point is that life slips away while we stay busy, so do what matters now.
verse.for_you: You are not lacking a plan, only a start. Set your aim on the very next step, the one that takes five minutes, and let the rest wait. The work is waiting for you to begin it.
verse.try_today: Pick the single task that takes the least time to start and do it now.
verse.scene_line: You are the father waiting for the right moment that will never arrive.
asks: What is the one task I can start in the next ten minutes?
How do I start before I feel fully ready?

verse.speaker: Vidura
verse.setting: Vidura counsels the sleepless King Dhritarashtra the night before the peace talks.
verse.sanskrit: निश्चित्य यः प्रक्रमते नान्तर्वसति कर्मणः / अवन्ध्यकालो वश्यात्मा स वै पण्डित उच्यते
verse.line: Decide, then begin. Don't stall halfway, don't waste time, and keep yourself steady.
verse.translation: One who begins only after deciding, does not stop halfway through the work, does not waste time and keeps himself in hand, is called wise.
verse.why: Decide calmly, act steadily, forgive freely, and know what real happiness is made of.

prasang.title: Vidura Niti: the wise and the fool
prasang.summary: Sleepless before the peace talks, King Dhritarashtra calls his half-brother Vidura for counsel. Vidura describes the marks of the wise and the fool, the faults that block progress, and the six joys of life.
prasang.lesson: Decide calmly, act steadily, forgive freely, and know what real happiness is made of.

verse.for_you: You want to move forward but the scale of it keeps you frozen. Vidura's point is that the moment of decision is enough to start. You do not need to see the whole path, only the first step.
verse.try_today: Pick one task and mark the exact hour you will begin it.

story.title: Building the bridge
story.story_hook: The army stood on the shore with no boats, until a quiet monkey said he knew how to build a bridge.
story.summary: Ram waits three days for the ocean to let him pass, then loses patience. The ocean reveals that Nala can build a bridge; Nala admits his skill and the whole army hauls trees and rocks for five days until the bridge reaches Lanka.
story.lesson: Big things get built by many hands, once someone admits they know how.

anchor.speaker: Nala
anchor.setting: The army is stuck at the ocean; Nala reveals he can build a bridge, which he had not mentioned.
anchor.sanskrit: समर्थश्चाप्यहं सेतुं कर्तुं वै वरुणालये। तस्मादद्यैव बध्नन्तु सेतुं वानरपुङ्गवाः॥
anchor.line: I can build this. Let's start today.
anchor.translation: I too am able to build a bridge across the ocean. So let the best of the monkeys start building it this very day.
anchor.why: Big things get built by many hands, once someone admits they know how.

prasang.title: Building the bridge
prasang.summary: Ram waits three days for the ocean to let him pass, then loses patience. The ocean reveals that Nala can build a bridge; Nala admits his skill and the whole army hauls trees and rocks for five days until the bridge reaches Lanka.
prasang.story_hook: The army stood on the shore with no boats, until a quiet monkey said he knew how to build a bridge.
prasang.lesson: Big things get built by many hands, once someone admits they know how.

story.hook_title: Ram's army stood on the shore with no boats, until a quiet monkey spoke up
story.teaser: Ram's army stood on the shore with no boats, until a quiet monkey spoke up
story.for_you: You have been waiting for the right conditions to begin your work, and the conditions may not feel ready. Nala did not wait for the ocean to change its mind. He simply stated his skill, and the army moved.
asks: What is the one task I know I can start?
Who else can help me move the first stone?
How do I stop waiting for the ocean to change?
